title: Simulator: the offline world and the fakes
tagline: A deterministic offline game the whole stack plays, with no game window and no keys
summary: World simulates MapleStory on a real map, tick by tick: her body by the client's movement engine, monsters with v83's AI, attacks, kills, EXP, drops, touches, knock-backs, respawns and other players. The fakes (FakeEyes, FakePlayer, a fake Clock) put it behind gamelab's own seams, so the unchanged stack runs on it, including the Lie Detector via FakePlayer.alarm_at. Scene sets replay moments of live recordings in it to check fixes before they go live.
details_md:
The simulator is a small, deterministic stand-in for MapleStory that the **whole** gamelab stack runs against with no game window and no key player. (*The stack* means gamelab's code above the game: perception's readers, localization, the planners, the hunter.) It plays on a real map (`localization.mapdata.MapModel`, from the game data), in map units, on a fake clock. Three parts:

- **The world** (`world.py`, `World`): her body, the monsters, attacks, kills, EXP, drops, touches, knock-backs, ropes, portals, pets and other players: "the game".
- **The fakes** (`fakes.py`): gamelab's existing seams faked over the world: `FakeEyes` for `perception.eyes.Eyes`, `FakePlayer` for `control.client` (the elevated key player), `Clock` for `time`; `patched` swaps them in and refuses anything that would reach the real game.
- **Scene sets** (`no_hit_scenes.py`, `hunt_scenes.py`): moments of live recordings put back into the world, to check a fix against what live play showed.

The sim-harness slice (`scenarios.py`, `harness.py`, `golden.py`) builds the stack on these and runs it.

**Words.** A *key plan* is a timed list of key down/up events for the key player; a *splice* replaces the rest of a running plan. A *seed* numbers one world (same seed, same run). A *golden trace* is a recorded scenario run later code must reproduce exactly; the *harness* runs many seeds and tabulates them.

### Time and determinism

The world keeps time in whole milliseconds on a **5 ms tick** (`TICK_MS`), and the game's own **30 ms step** (`STEP_MS`, from `motion.body.STEP`) falls at a phase drawn from the seed. Keys are events in a sorted queue (`Event`), and the world only runs forward when a fake asks (`World.advance`: every fake look, glance, message read or cancel), so its state depends only on the key events, never on how often the stack looked. Random draws are keyed by what they are for, the seed and the tick (`World.chance`: `Random(f"{what}:{seed}:{ms}")`), and each optional knob has its own generator, so switching one off leaves the other draws unchanged.

### What happens to a key

The game sees a key half a step (15 ms) before the measured medians (`body.Lags`: arrow pressed 66 ms, let go 68 ms, jump 65 ms) and acts at its next 30 ms step, so on average it acts those medians after the key. On the ground an arrow accelerates her by the engine's rule (`body.ground_step`) and letting go brakes her; a jump gets the "kick" (`body.takeoff`); in the air she flies `body.fly`'s arc, re-flown whenever the arrow the game sees changes. Walls stop her by the client's rule plus foothold group 0's walls (`Realism.zero_walls`). Up grabs a rope, down on a rope's top climbs down it, jump with down held drops her through a platform.

An attack's timeline:

| When (after the key) | What |
|---|---|
| 65 ms (`JUMP_LAG`) | it picks its target from where she is then: the claw's swipe up close, else the star's band search (from a jump: `AIR_PICK` 'search'); then the line to the star's pick is checked (`sight_stop`) |
| 290 ms (`DAMAGE_SHOWS_MS`) | the server's damage: HP off, or the kill, her EXP and (2 s later) drops |
| 520 ms (`STAR_DELAY_MS`) | the star lands: the monster's flinch, push-back and its chase of her (aggro) |
| 0.75 s + distance / 1490 | a killed monster stops being drawn alive and plays its death (`Realism.dies_late`) |

### Monsters and touches

Monsters walk as the v83 client's AI moves them (each decision a whole number of 90 ms AI steps, 1-3 s long), turning 20 units in from their platform's ends (`WALK_EDGE`); Slimes jump (`SimJumper`). A hit makes the monster chase her for 180-240 s. A monster touches her when the box of the frame it shows meets a 50-unit vertical line over her feet (the client's touch test). A touch leaves her invulnerable for 1.5 s and is a MISS (her evasion) or takes HP (a share of the monster's touch damage, or meowdb's formula with her DEF), knocks her back 270 units/s out and up (not on a rope), and may make her pet drink a potion.

### Knobs

- `Noise`: the real game's and perception's errors (missed stars, spread lags, lost taps, detector misses, hidden name tag or minimap dot...), all off by default.
- `Realism`: what isn't known of the game and how busy the map is (respawn passes, other players, drops, inventory, walls, knock, aggro...); the defaults are the simulator's own world.
- `Her`: the character (`LEVEL_19` ... `LEVEL_25`, `MAGE_32`, `HER_35`).

The world keeps **its own truth** apart from the stack's beliefs (invulnerability 1.5 s in the world, 1.45 s in the stack's `perception.touches.INVULNERABLE_S`; her true walking speed whatever her planner assumes), so a wrong belief shows up as a cost instead of being hidden.

### The fakes

`FakeEyes` draws each look as a blank frame carrying a `Screen` record (monsters, drops, her heading, touch popups); the fake detectors read that record, not pixels. Monsters' HP bars and her EXP, HP and level numbers are real pixels, read by the real readers. Her place comes straight from the world (`TRUE_PLACE`). `FakePlayer` plays each key plan's events on the world, one plan after another, with cancels, splices and the **Lie Detector**: with `alarm_at` set, the running plan stops then, and afterwards only what the real player's rule (`control.player.alarm_refusal`) lets through plays: pet food, her retreat's moves for 12 s, the solver's cursor and OK clicks.

modules.tagline: The game simulated on a real map, tick by tick, driven by key events
modules.summary: World holds her (position, speed, mode, HP, MP, EXP, inventory), the monsters (SimMonster, SimJumper), drops, pets and other players, and runs them forward tick by tick when a fake asks (advance). Keys come in as timed events; the game sees them after measured lags and acts at its 30 ms steps. The comment above each constant says where its value comes from (a measurement, the game data or a v83 client source) and which ones are guesses; Noise, Realism and Her switch the unknowns and errors on and off.
modules.details_md:
The file is long (4.2k lines) but plain, top to bottom:

1. **Constants with their evidence** (lines 150-975): each under a comment saying where it came from (recordings, telemetry, game data, HeavenClient/RustMS, meowdb) and what it was before.
2. **Knob dataclasses**: `Noise` (game and perception errors, all off by default), `Realism` (unknowns and crowd), `Camp`, `Her` and the presets `LEVEL_19`, `LEVEL_23`, `LEVEL_24`, `LEVEL_25`, `MAGE_32` (plus the `HER_35` dict).
3. **Monster game data**: `Frame`, `MobInfo`, `mob_info` (read from `Mob/<id>.img`, cached as JSON), and the damage maths: `touch_damage`, `stars_to_kill`, `hits_of`, `evade_chance`, `game_hit_chance`, `push_chance`.
4. **Monsters**: `SimMonster` (walkers) and `SimJumper` (monsters that jump), with `JumpSpace` and `end_link`.
5. **Small records**: `Drop`, `SimPet`, `Rival`, `Event`.
6. **`World`**: set-up, time, the tick, keys, her motion, touches, attacks and kills, the map's respawn pass, other players, loot and pets, and "what can be seen".

### One tick (`World._tick`, every 5 ms)

1. Handle every queued event due by now (`_handle`): key down/up, release, "seen" (the game noticing a key), "liftoff", "aim", "star", "struck", "loot", "map_tick", rival and camp events, test callbacks (`call_at`).
2. Move her: `_ground` (at each 30 ms game step `body.ground_step` sets her speed for the step and she glides 1/6 of it per tick; past a platform's end she flies off unless a wall rises there), `_air` (the flight's precomputed path, re-flown when the arrow the game sees changes; she lands, grabs a rope or falls out of the map), or `_climb`.
3. Up held at an exit portal (within `PORTAL_BOX`) ends the run (`SimLeftMap`).
4. `_touch`, the harness's `_closeness` and `_idleness` counters, MP regeneration, the path log every 100 ms, her pets every 50 ms.

`World.advance(clock_t)` runs ticks to the clock and raises `SimDied`, `SimLeftMap` or `SimFellOut` once the run is over.

### Monsters

A `SimMonster`'s motion is a list of segments (stand, walk left, walk right) drawn lazily from its own generator; `ghost()` copies it (and its generators) to look ahead without disturbing it. Decisions follow v83's AI: `AI_STEP` 90 ms, an idle decision of `(r + 1000) // 90` steps with r uniform in 0-1999 (1.0-3.0 s), a third each stand/left/right; chasing, `(r + 800) // 90` with r in 0-399, at her (or on past her up to `AGGRO_PASS`, 100 units). A hit whose damage (after the monster's defence) reaches the game data's `pushed` pushes it `KNOCK_MOB` (about 21 units: 130 units/s slowing at 400 units/s squared), and it stands in its hit1 frame for `FLINCH_S` (0.6 s). Its touch body is the lt/rb box of the frame it shows, turned the way it faces. A `SimJumper` (a monster with a jump action, `MapModel.mob_hops`: Tree Dungeon's Slimes) is stepped event by event: AI steps, walk ends, jumps, landings, hit ends.

### Attacks

`_pressed` refuses an attack key on a rope (`ROPE_REFUSAL` on the message bar), ignores it inside the 0.73 s attack lock (`ATTACK_LOCK`), spends MP for Lucky Seven (`_cast`) or refuses with too little, and queues "aim" at `JUMP_LAG`. `_aim` picks; `_attack` applies damage at `DAMAGE_SHOWS_MS`; `_struck` (at `STAR_DELAY_MS`) flinches, pushes and aggroes; `_kill` gives EXP (`model.mob_exp`), queues drops 2 s later and, only with `respawn_tick` 0, its own respawn. The magician's Magic Claw has its own path (`_press_magic`, `magic_pick`, `_aim_magic`, `_attack_magic`): no line check, ground only, two hits of 157-181 a cast.

### The map's life

With `Realism.respawn_tick` (default `TICK_S`, 7.115 s), `_map_tick` refills the map to its cap (`MapModel.mob_cap`, the server's formula) at random spawn points with no monster within `SPAWN_CLEAR` (100 units), as OrionAlpha's `LifePool.tryCreateMob` does. Other players are a roaming `Rival` and fixed or coming-and-going `Camp`s, whose kills give her no EXP (unless `shared_exp`) and whose drops she can't take for `rival_owns` s. Pets (`Realism.pets`) trail her and take drops they walk over.

### The game's windows

The backslash opens the KEY BINDINGS window (keys do nothing while open), Esc closes it or opens the MENU, her stats key toggles her stat window, her chat key her chat box: for the stack's key, stat and chat checks.

### What the fakes read

`her()`, `visible_monsters()` (killed ones drawn alive until the star lands, then fading), `drawn_bar()`, `dying_at()`, `live_drops()`, `recent_messages()`, `mp_drawn()` (MP shown 0.29 s late), `others_at()`, `binding_view()`, and the harness's logs (`attack_log`, `touch_log`, `kill_log`...).

key_items.name: World
key_items.signature: class World: def __init__(self, model: MapModel, keys: GameKeys, start: tuple[int, float], seed: int = 1, monsters="all", hp=1.0, inventory_full=False, facing=RIGHT, origin=0.0, drops=(), hanging=None, noise=None, realism=None, step_phase=None, character=LEVEL_19)
key_items.summary: The simulated game: her standing on platform start[0] at x start[1] (or hanging on a rope), the map's monsters at their spawn points (or a given list), drops lying, and every log the harness reads.
key_items.details_md: Each knob draws from its own generator (`rival:`, `drops:`, `camps:`, `ticks:`, `mix:`, `takers:`, `pets:`, `expiry:` + seed; each monster's chase `chase:<seed>:<i>`), so the world with a knob off is the same as without it. `step_phase` (the ms of the game's first 30 ms step) is drawn from `step:<seed>`. Her walk and climb are her truth (`her_shoe`, `her_climb`), not her planner's. With `respawn_tick` on, the monsters over the map's cap start dead and the first pass comes at a drawn phase.

key_items.name: World.advance
key_items.summary: Runs whole 5 ms ticks up to clock time clock_t; raises SimLeftMap, SimFellOut or SimDied once the run is over, so the next look finds it ended.
key_items.details_md: The fakes call it before every look, glance or plan check: the world is lazy and only moves when observed, which is why the result doesn't depend on how often it is observed.

key_items.name: World.chance
key_items.signature: def chance(self, what: str, ms: int | None = None) -> float
key_items.summary: A noise draw in [0, 1) for `what` at tick `ms` (now by default): random.Random(f"{what}:{seed}:{ms}").random(), the same every run whatever was looked at before.
key_items.details_md: The evade and damage rolls of a touch, the claw's stance, a band's tie, a push, a miss, the death watch's sighting, the looks' misses and the air pick's noise all draw here, each named (`evade`, `damage`, `stance`, `band`, `push:<idx>`, `see:<idx>`...). That is what makes a run reproducible and lets a look be added or dropped without moving later draws.

key_items.name: World._tick
key_items.summary: One 5 ms tick: handle due events, move her (ground, air or rope), portals, touches, closeness and idleness counters, MP regeneration, the path log and her pets.

key_items.name: World._pressed
key_items.signature: def _pressed(self, action: str, at: float) -> None
key_items.summary: A key going down, as the game takes it: arrows seen after Lags.on (or swallowed during an attack with Realism.lock_arrows), jump lifted off at the step after Lags.jump (lost in the air), drop-through with down, attacks (lock, rope refusal, MP, darts), rope grabs, pick-up, potion and pet food.
key_items.details_md: An attack key outside the 0.73 s lock queues an `aim` event at `JUMP_LAG` (65 ms). With `Realism.lock_arrows`, an arrow pressed less than `ARROW_LOCK` (0.719 s) after an attack's key is seen only `ARROW_HELD` (0.77 s) after that key, and only if still held.

key_items.name: World._ground
key_items.summary: Her on the ground: at each game step body.ground_step sets her speed toward the arrow the game sees (or brakes), then she glides a sixth of the step per tick; past a platform's end she flies off unless a wall rises there.

key_items.name: World._air
key_items.summary: Her in the air along the precomputed body.fly path; re-flown from where she is when the steering arrow changes (none during a knock); lands, grabs a rope with up held, or falls out of the map below its lowest floor (SimFellOut).

key_items.name: World._touch
key_items.summary: Checks the monsters on nearby platforms against her body (default HER_TOUCH: a line 50 tall at her x) using each monster's current frame box; skips newborns still fading in and while she is invulnerable.

key_items.name: World._hit_by
key_items.signature: def _hit_by(self, m: SimMonster, mx: float) -> None
key_items.summary: A touch: invulnerability for Realism.invulnerable (1.5 s), MISS by evade_chance, else HP off by touch_damage, death at 0, her pet's potion, and the knock-back flight (not on a rope unless Realism.rope_knocks).
key_items.details_md: The knock pushes 270 units/s away from the monster and 270 up (`KNOCK_VX`, `KNOCK_VY`); with `KNOCK_ADDS` the sideways push adds to her own speed without exceeding 270, and with `KNOCK_LANDS_WALKING` she lands at no more than her walk speed: about 73 units in the air and a 14-unit slide from standing.

key_items.name: World._aim
key_items.signature: def _aim(self, key_ms: int, skill: bool = False, tag: str = "", step: int | None = None) -> None
key_items.summary: The attack starts (65 ms after its key) and picks its target from where she is: on the ground a random claw stance's swipe, else the star's band search; in the air the search from her feet (AIR_PICK 'search'); then the line check (sight_stop). Queues the damage at DAMAGE_SHOWS_MS.
key_items.details_md: With `AIR_TURN_SAME_STEP`, an arrow the game acted on at the same step as the attack key turns her too late: the attack goes the way she faced before. Ties within a band are drawn at random (the client's order by when each monster entered the map is unknown). A stopped star hits nothing and no other monster takes it.

key_items.name: World._attack
key_items.signature: def _attack(self, facing: str, m: SimMonster | None, swipe: bool, stop: tuple | None = None, skill: bool = False, how: tuple | None = None, key_ms: int | None = None) -> None
key_items.summary: The server's damage, 290 ms after the key: a miss (Noise.miss), HP off in stars (a claw swipe 0.2), and either a 'struck' event when the star lands (520 ms) or the kill.

key_items.name: World._kill
key_items.signature: def _kill(self, m: SimMonster, mx: float, what: str, key_ms: int | None = None, bar: float = 1.0) -> None
key_items.summary: A kill: drawn alive until her star lands (DIE_LANDS_S + distance / DIE_FLIGHT), EXP from model.mob_exp, drops queued DROP_DELAY (2 s) later, drop-takers scheduled, and (only with respawn_tick 0) its own respawn Realism.respawn s later; called from _attack at the damage's time instead of a 'struck'.

key_items.name: World._map_tick
key_items.summary: The map's respawn pass every TICK_S (7.115 s): fills to the cap (MapModel.mob_cap) at randomly ordered spawn points with no monster within SPAWN_CLEAR (100 units), as OrionAlpha's LifePool.tryCreateMob.
key_items.details_md: Monster positions for the clearance test come from `ghost()` copies, because looking at a chasing monster would otherwise advance its own walk.

key_items.name: SimMonster
key_items.summary: A walking monster: lazily drawn motion segments from its own rng, v83 AI decisions, the chase after a hit (aggro), the push-back and flinch, and its body from the game data's frame boxes.

key_items.name: SimJumper
key_items.summary: A monster that jumps (Tree Dungeon's Slimes), moved event by event as v83's Mob::think, think_jump and jump: a jump in one idle decision of five (JUMP_IDLE), at a rising wall within 40 units ahead, off its platform's ends, and, chasing her while she is over a higher floor of another group, one AI step in three (JUMP_CHASE).
key_items.details_md: Its history is a list of segments (`stand`, `walk`, `press`, `hit`, `air`), kept `JUMPER_KEEP_S` (10 s) back so a look a little back in time still works.

inputs: a MapModel (localization.mapdata) for the map's platforms, ropes, walls, portals, spawns, EXP and caps
her GameKeys (maplehelper.config), mapped to actions by _actions
timed key events, releases and clicks from FakePlayer (World.key, release_all, click, withdraw_from)
the clock's time from FakeEyes and FakePlayer (World.advance)
Noise, Realism and Her settings from the scenario or harness
monster frames, HP, accuracy and touch damage from the game data (Mob/<id>.img via gamedata), cached as JSON
outputs: what can be seen, for FakeEyes: her place and mode, visible monsters with poses, bars and fades, drops, messages, MP as drawn, others' places, the key-binding and stat windows' state
SimDied / SimLeftMap / SimFellOut when a run ends
logs for the harness and tests: attack_log, pick_log, touch_log, land_log, knock_log, kill_log, death_log, path_log, idle_log, climb_log, grab_log, aim_log and a text log
summary(): her end state for the golden trace

files_io.what: each monster's game-data facts (frames, HP, PDDamage, accuracy, pushed) cached by mob_info; written whole through a .part file and os.replace because harness workers read it too

files_io.path: Mob/<mob id>.img (the game data copy, via gamedata.canvas)
files_io.what: read by _read_mob when the cache is missing or older than its fields

modules.concurrency: None of its own: single-threaded and lazy, run forward only when a fake asks (advance). Harness workers in other processes share the monster cache files.

tunables.name: STEP_MS
tunables.meaning: the game's step: it acts on keys and sets her ground speed every 30 ms

tunables.name: ATTACK_LOCK
tunables.meaning: attack keys (and jump keys) pressed inside the last attack's lock are ignored (COMBAT.attack_lock_ms)

tunables.name: ARROW_HELD / ARROW_LOCK
tunables.meaning: with Realism.lock_arrows, an arrow pressed within ARROW_LOCK of an attack key is seen only ARROW_HELD after it

tunables.name: JUMP_TAKEN_LATE
tunables.meaning: a jump key pressed in the air is lost (the harsher choice for plans)

tunables.name: HER_TOUCH
tunables.meaning: her touch body: a line 50 tall at her x, the client's test

tunables.name: INVULNERABLE
tunables.meaning: invulnerability after a touch, MISS or damage

tunables.name: TOUCH_SHARE / TOUCH_SPREAD
tunables.meaning: a touch takes 0.68 of the monster's PADamage, give or take 70% (when her DEF isn't set)

tunables.name: DEFENCE
tunables.meaning: her DEF in meowdb's touch formula for the Tree Dungeon characters

tunables.name: EVADE_ACC
tunables.meaning: evasion chance = EVADE_ACC / the monster's accuracy (without Her.avoid)

tunables.name: KNOCK_VX, KNOCK_VY
tunables.meaning: her knock-back push out and up, units/s

tunables.name: AI_STEP
tunables.meaning: the monster AI's step

tunables.name: IDLE_THINK_MS / CHASE_THINK_MS
tunables.meaning: decision length: (r + least) // 90 steps, r uniform in 0..span-1

tunables.name: AGGRO_S / AGGRO_PASS
tunables.meaning: how long a hit monster chases her, and how far it walks past her before turning

tunables.name: WALK_EDGE
tunables.meaning: a walker turns this far along its end foothold from its platform's end (localization.monsters)

tunables.name: KNOCK_MOB_V / KNOCK_MOB_DECEL
tunables.meaning: a hit monster's push (about 21 units over 0.33 s)

tunables.name: STAR_DAMAGE / CLAW
tunables.meaning: a star's damage range; a claw swipe is 0.2 of a star

tunables.name: HITS
tunables.meaning: first-map monsters' HP in stars; other kinds by stars_to_kill

tunables.name: LUCKY_SEVEN / CAST_MP / MP_REGEN
tunables.meaning: Lucky Seven in stars, its MP cost, her MP regeneration

tunables.name: AIR_PICK
tunables.meaning: how an attack from a jump picks: the star's search from her feet (also 'widening', 'area', 'v83')

tunables.name: TICK_S / SPAWN_CLEAR
tunables.meaning: the map's respawn pass period, and the clearance a spawn point needs

tunables.name: RESPAWN
tunables.meaning: per-monster respawn delay when respawn_tick is 0 (a guess)

tunables.name: DROP_DELAY / DROP_LIFE / PICK_REACH
tunables.meaning: drops land 2 s after a kill, lie 180 s, are picked within 15 units

tunables.name: DIE_LANDS_S / DIE_FLIGHT
tunables.meaning: a killed monster is drawn alive until key + 0.75 s + distance / 1490

tunables.name: SPAWN_FADE_S / NEWBORN_SOLID_S
tunables.meaning: a newborn fades in over this and touches nothing until then

tunables.name: CLAW_HIT / CLAW_LOCK_S / CLAW_SHOWS_S
tunables.meaning: the magician's Magic Claw: hit damage (two a cast), lock, and when the hit shows

tunables.name: NEAR_SEEN / OFF_SEEN
tunables.meaning: with Noise.near_seen set (the harness's near-misses world): the detector's chance of finding a monster by distance on her platform (0.39 within 25 units ... 0.93 past 150), and on another

tunables.name: TAKE_RATE / EXPIRE_PASS_S
tunables.meaning: others take her drops at this rate after her ownership; expiry passes this far apart (both guesses)

tunables.name: JUMPERS
tunables.meaning: monsters with a jump action jump (SimJumper); False walks them like the others

tunables.name: DIE_LOST_S
tunables.meaning: with dies_late, the looks lose a dying monster this long after its death animation starts (the detector has no die1 pictures)

tunables.name: DEATH_SEEN / DEATH_SEEN_AFTER
tunables.meaning: the fake death watch sees 83% of deaths, 0.14 s after the death animation begins (live: 118 of 142)

tunables.name: POPUP_S
tunables.meaning: how long a touch's MISS or damage popup shows over her (v83's 400 ms opaque + 600 fading; unconfirmed in this game)

tunables.name: AIR_TURN_SAME_STEP
tunables.meaning: an arrow acted on in the air at the same 30 ms step as an attack's key turns her too late for it

decisions.what: Arrows pressed during an attack are swallowed (Realism.lock_arrows; ARROW_HELD 0.77 s, 0.835 until that day's review)
decisions.why: In game, chains sent right after a throw first moved her about 0.79 s after the attack key

decisions.what: The star's line is checked by the v83 line (reach.LINE)
decisions.why: The user saw her own platform stop her stars in game

decisions.what: Damage applied at the server's DAMAGE_SHOWS_MS (0.29 s) instead of at the star's release (STAR_DELAY_MS)
decisions.why: Live, a kill's EXP gain showed 0.15-0.46 s after the key

decisions.what: AIR_PICK 'search' the default for attacks from a jump, with fitted air noise (TREE_AIR)
decisions.why: 'widening' counted live throws as hits that weren't, hiding what keeping clear gains

decisions.what: A touch on a rope leaves her on it (Realism.rope_knocks False)
decisions.why: Live on 2026-10-26, 11 of 11 hits on a rope left her on it

decisions.what: The respawn cap by the server's formula (MapModel.mob_cap)
decisions.why: The user: "Let's use the formula... we don't know how many mobs are on the map at any given time"

decisions.what: Respawn by the map's pass (respawn_tick) in every world

modules.title: The fakes
modules.tagline: Fake eyes, a fake key player and a fake clock over the world, with guards
modules.summary: FakeEyes answers perception's questions from the world (looks, glances, monsters, bars, drops, numbers, windows), FakePlayer plays key plans on it as the real key player would (cancels, splices, the Lie Detector via alarm_at), and Clock makes time pass only when something sleeps or looks. patched swaps them into gamelab for a run and makes anything that would touch the real game or gamelab/lab raise SimViolation.
modules.details_md:
`fakes.py` fakes the three seams between gamelab and the outside world, so the unchanged stack runs on a `World`.

### `Clock`

Replaces `time.monotonic`, `sleep`, `time`, `perf_counter` and `strftime`. It starts at `START` (10,000 s; `time.time()` reads `EPOCH` plus elapsed). Nothing takes time but sleeps and the fakes' own calls, each charged a documented cost (`LOOK_S` 0.10 s a look, `GLANCE_S` 0.035 s, `DETECT_S` 0.03 s, `DETECT_WIDE_S` 0.25 s, `LOOT_S` 0.02 s a strip, `MESSAGES_S` 0.4 s...): a loop that only looked would otherwise never see time move. Options: `limit` (raises `SimTimeout`, a `BaseException` so `except Exception` recovery loops can't swallow it), `pace` (also sleep in real time, to watch on the mini-map), `think` (charge the stack's real computing time, measured with the real `perf_counter`) and `reads` (charge it at every clock read). `frames` calls a function at every game frame the clock passes (the continuous feed's `SyncFeed.tick` at 60 Hz).

### `FakeEyes` (a subclass of `perception.eyes.Eyes`)

Each `look()` runs the world to the clock, draws the screen as the world is then into an `Observation` stamped as taken at `now + LOOK_LAG`, then sleeps `LOOK_S` on the fake clock. `observe()` is the same picture with no cost, for the continuous feed. A frame is a blank half-size (540x960) array of sky colour, viewed as `Frame`, with a `Screen` record attached: monsters as `perception.mobs.Mob` (position, size, facing, pose `move`/`stand`/`hit1`, fade-in alpha), drops as `perception.loot.Item`, her heading as a `heading.Reading`, and touch popups. `FakeDetector` and `FakeLoot` "find" what is wholly inside the searched rows or box. Real pixels are drawn where real readers read them: HP bars (`hud.draw_hp_bar`, read by the inherited `Eyes.bar`, cached by the box's bytes), her EXP number (`exp_number.draw` with the game's glyphs, levels carried with the EXP table: `shown_exp`), her HP and level numbers, the KEY BINDINGS window and her stat window (`_capture`, at 1366x768). With `TRUE_PLACE` her place is the world's own, handed over as a `localization.locate.Located` with confidence 1.0 (her dot only while `Noise.unfound`).

What a look misses is decided in `_unseen`, all from the world's seeded chances: a death animation after `DIE_LOST_S`, a newborn still too faint (`Noise.spawn_found`), a hit monster hiding under its numbers (`Noise.hit_hidden`; the magician's `SimMagic.hidden`), the detector's misses by distance on her platform (`Noise.near_seen`, in spells: `near_spell`) or on another (`off_seen`), and plain `detect_miss`. `FakeDeaths` and `FakeTouches` stand in for the death watch and the touch watch; `FakePetCare` reads the pet's fullness straight off the world.

### `FakePlayer`

Implements `client.send / submit / wait / done / cancel / splice / taken / can_splice` and the alarm calls. A plan is validated with the real `control.player.validate`, starts `START_LATENCY` (10 ms) after it is handed over and after the plans before it, and its events are pushed onto the world as timed key events; every key still held is released at its end. `cancel` withdraws a plan not started (one due at that very moment counts as not started) or cuts a running one (release all, the next plan 10 ms later). `splice` withdraws the running plan's later keys from the moment it takes over (at its `at_ms` or when the player sees it, `SPLICE_SEEN_S` 17 ms after hand-over), adjusting held keys; one the player would only see after the plan ended is never taken.

**The Lie Detector** (`alarm_at`): from that clock time `alarm_up()` is true and `check_alarm()` raises `client.LieDetectorAlarm`. `_cutoff` decides each plan's fate as the real player would: a plan running at the sighting stops there (answered with `alarm.LIE_DETECTOR_ERROR`); one starting later plays only if its kind is in `alarm.PLAN_KINDS` (pet food, retreat, and the solver's `lie_cursor` and `lie_ok` clicks) and the real `player.alarm_refusal` lets it through; a `retreat` plan is cut at `RETREAT_WINDOW_S` (12 s) after the sighting. `page` and `keep_recent` are recorded, not executed.

### `patched`

The context manager that puts all this in place for a run and restores everything after: `time.*`, `client.*`, `alarm.page` and `keep_recent`; every `Path` under `gamelab/lab` in loaded gamelab modules (globals and function defaults) moved to a temporary folder; write guards on `open`, `io.open`, `os.open`, `os.replace/rename/remove/unlink/mkdir/rmdir/utime` for paths under the real lab; and `maplehelper.win32.send_key`, the `gamelab.window` calls and `analysis.recordings.record` replaced by functions that raise `SimViolation`.

modules.title: No-hit scenes
modules.tagline: Eleven moments of attacks at nothing from live recordings, replayed in the world
modules.summary: Each Scene puts her and the on-screen monsters back where a failsafe recording of 2026-11-04/05 had them, monsters walking their recorded rails until she hits them, then runs the full stack for about 15 fake seconds. measures, fault_shows and Scene.solved say whether the recording's fault reproduces and whether a fix solves it in the user's terms.
modules.details_md:
**Why it exists.** The failsafe's recordings of 2026-11-04 and 11-05 showed her attacks hitting nothing in a handful of recurring situations. Whole-run harness tables can't tell whether a fix helps: per-seed spread is about 64 EXP a minute, so a +10 effect needs about 160 seeds. The user asked to "create scene in simulation to verify they work/solve the problem". Each scene puts a few seconds of a recording back into the world and runs the full stack (about 1.2 s of real time a run). Scenes are not in `scenarios.SCENARIOS`: no golden trace, no effect on other runs.

**A scene** (`Scene`) starts about 0.15 s before the look of the clip's first attack of its cause: her platform and x, facing, HP, MP, invulnerability left (`inv`), attack lock left (`locked`), the failsafe's count of attacks at nothing so far (`misses`), other players' minimap dots (`others`, as `Camp`s that hunt nothing), and the monsters on screen (`Mob`) with their HP bars and whether they already chase her. The monsters near her walk **on rails**: `(seconds, way)` stretches read off the recording's timeline, until her first hit on that monster, then the world's own AI (`_RailWalker`, `_RailJumper` swap in by changing the monster's class in `_place`).

**The world** is the harness's `loop-grind` scenario on Tree Dungeon (preset `crowd`, attack policy `choice`) in the standard thief's worlds (`WORLD`: zero-walls, near-misses, walkers, spawn-fade, map-drops, drop-takers, near-misses-exact) with her at level 35 (`HER_35`), a star's miss chance of 0.04 (`MISS`, measured at a Green; the standard world's 0.275 is the first map's at level 19), no respawns within the scene (`respawn_tick` 0, `respawn` 600 s) and 15 s long by default. `scenario_of` also sets her stack as it was then: her facing, her target (`chooser.primary`), her belief of who chases her (`_she_hit`) and the failsafe's count (`_counted`). `script` adds events, such as another player's kill at a given second (`_strangers_kill`).

**Judging.** `run_scene` runs a scene with the harness's measured look costs, captures telemetry, and returns `measures`: attacks, attacks at nothing (outcomes `nothing`, `stopped`, `miss`), the same within the recording's span, first hit, first star, claw swipes, when the target died, EXP, touches, knock-offs, the longest stand with a monster within 60 units (`_watch_stand`), MP spent. `fault_shows` says whether runs reproduce the recording's fault (by `Scene.fault`, else the runs' mean attacks at nothing in the recording's span at least `FAULT_SHARE` 0.6 of the recording's count, and of what the runs keyed); `Scene.solved` lists what "solved" means in the user's words (fewer attacks at nothing, first hit sooner, no standing still, the target killed, no less EXP), each about half of master's numbers. `SHIFTS` are small changes the frames can't rule out (rails 0.1 s late or early, her place 6 units either way); `over_shifts` counts on how many the verdicts hold.

**The 11 scenes** cover: too close in front (`too_close_081701`, `too_close_111448`), at a wall's foot (`wall_foot_231613`), monsters walking past her (`walked_past_080032`, `walked_past_080939`), from below (`from_below_233732`, `from_below_234441`), another player's kill (`stranger_dead_080929`, `stranger_dying_080929`), a throw at her own kill (`own_kill_235621`) and a failsafe firing that was then ignored (`ignored_235621`).

**Where they stand.** `tests/test_no_hit_scenes.py` keeps the scenes not yet solved in `OPEN` (strict expected failures): 8 of the 11, four whose fault still shows (`FAULT`: 111448, 080939, stranger_dying, own_kill) and four whose fault is gone but not every solved condition holds.

modules.title: Hunt journeys
modules.tagline: Live journeys between platforms (2026-11-05) replayed in the world with the full stack
modules.summary: Each case from tests/fixtures/hunt_journeys_2026-11-05.json becomes a short grind: her start where the journey set off, the monsters seen on the way, her patrol round frozen. run_journey reports the platforms she stood on, her first attack's platform and whether she got where the live journey went, to judge stopping at landings (behavior.targeting.stay_or_go).
modules.details_md:
**Why it exists.** The user, 2026-11-05, on why she goes down to the low platforms and stays, and skips busy areas when travelling ("when you travel to another platform, especially when down jumping, you seem to skip an area with large amount of mobs which could potentially more beneficial"). The fix (`behavior.targeting.stay_or_go`: ask, at a landing inside a chain of moves, whether to stop there) is judged on real journeys.

**What it does.** The journeys of the tours of 2026-11-05 are stored in `tests/fixtures/hunt_journeys_2026-11-05.json` (`JOURNEYS`). Each case has where the journey set off (`start`), the platforms it passed, its target or the pile it went for (`kind` "loot"), the monsters the perception service saw on the way (`mobs`), her patrol round and its rate, and how long it took live (`seconds`).

`scenario_of(case, seed)` turns one into a world: the harness's `loop-grind` scenario on Tree Dungeon (`scenarios.TREE`) in the `crowd` preset with the worlds in `WORLD` (the thief's standard plus `live-floors`, which puts her at level 35: `HER_35` with Lucky Seven's stars 166-333 and a star's miss chance of 0.04; its other players are dropped here), only the monsters on the platforms it passed (and the target's), no other players and no respawn within it (`respawn_tick` 0, `respawn` 600 s), lasting the live time plus `AFTER_S` (8 s). Its run function builds the real hunter, navigator, tour and `Grind`, freezes the patrol's plan to the journey's round and rate (`replan` disabled), has her first ground decision find her already visiting her start place with the round's first stop as her stop, and for a loot journey seeds a remembered pile of mesos at its target.

`run_journey` runs it with the harness's measured look costs, captures telemetry, and returns the platforms she stood on in order (`path`, from `scene` records), the platform of her first attack, whether she got where the journey went (`got_there`), her kills and touches, how many times the landing question was asked (log lines with "at a landing"), and the log. `tests/test_stay_or_go.py` runs three of the fixture's 11 journeys with the question off and on (`GAMELAB_STAY_OR_GO` 0 and 1: the question is off by default until a live trial reports).

Like the no-hit scenes, these are not in `scenarios.SCENARIOS`: no golden, no effect on other runs.

flows.title: How a key plan moves her in the world
flows.summary: The stack's key plan goes through the faked client into timed world events; the world only runs when something looks.
flows.trigger: The stack (Actions, Mover, Navigator) calls control.client.send, patched to FakePlayer.send

steps.text: Validates the plan with the real player's rules, records it in the Trace, and schedules it to start 10 ms after hand-over and after the plans before it.
Pushes each event onto the world at start + lead + its ms (World.key, World.click), skipping a down of a key already held, and a release of every key at the plan's end.
The stack's next look (or glance) first runs the world up to the fake clock: World.advance calls World._tick every 5 ms of the way.

Each due key event becomes a press or release of an action (her GameKeys mapped by _actions); _pressed queues a 'seen' event when the game will notice the arrow (Lags.on less half a step, at its next 30 ms step).
The game now sees the arrow: she turns that way (in the air, maybe not: Noise.air_turn_lost); the arrow pressed last counts.
At each game step body.ground_step accelerates her toward the seen arrow or brakes her; she glides a sixth of the step per 5 ms tick, and flies off an unwalled end.

Back in the same look, the screen is drawn from the world as it now stands (her true place via TRUE_PLACE, the monsters and drops into the frame's Screen) for the stack's perception; then the look's LOOK_S is charged to the clock.

flows.title: An attack, from key to kill
flows.summary: The world resolves an attack on the game's timeline: pick at 65 ms, damage at 290 ms, the star landing at 520 ms, the death drawn later.
flows.trigger: An attack or Lucky Seven key event reaches the world outside the attack lock

steps.text: Starts the 0.73 s lock, spends a cast's MP if it's Lucky Seven (or refuses: too little MP, no darts, on a rope), and queues 'aim' at JUMP_LAG (65 ms).

Picks the target from where she is now: a claw stance's swipe up close, else the star's band search; from a jump, the search from her feet with the fitted air noise. The line to a star's pick is checked (sight_stop). Queues 'star' at DAMAGE_SHOWS_MS (290 ms).
Applies the server's damage: a miss (Noise.miss), HP off in stars, or the kill; a hit that doesn't kill queues 'struck' at STAR_DELAY_MS (520 ms).
The star lands: the monster's damage numbers (it may hide under them), its flinch and push-back if the damage reaches its 'pushed', and its chase of her for 180-240 s.

If the damage kills it, _attack calls this at the 290 ms mark instead of queuing 'struck': EXP from the map's table, the monster drawn alive until the star lands (0.75 s + distance / 1490), drops landing 2 s later; by default it comes back at a later pass of the map's respawn.
Looks show the hurt monster's HP bar as real pixels (read by Eyes.bar), the dying monster until DIE_LOST_S, then nothing; FakeDeaths reports the death on 83% of deaths.

flows.title: A monster touches her
flows.summary: Every tick the world checks monsters' frame boxes against her touch line; a touch costs HP or is a MISS, knocks her back and may make her pet drink.
flows.trigger: World._tick, every 5 ms, when she isn't invulnerable

steps.text: Collects monsters on platforms near her (and jumpers in the air), skips newborns fading in, and tests each one's current frame box against her body (default a line 50 tall at her x).
Starts 1.5 s of invulnerability; draws a MISS by evade_chance, else takes touch_damage of her HP; at 0 HP she dies (SimDied at the next advance).
Her pet drinks a potion if she's under its warning, at least 0.2 s after its last, and isn't too hungry.
Unless she's on a rope, she is knocked away and up at 270 units/s (adding to her own sideways speed, landing at her walk's speed at most), unsteerable until she lands.
The next frames carry the touch's popup (MISS or the damage number) for 1 s; the touch watch tells it once, as the stack's own reads it live.

flows.title: The Lie Detector in a simulated hunt
flows.summary: A scenario sets FakePlayer.alarm_at; from then on the fake player refuses and cuts plans by the real elevated player's own rule (control.player.alarm_refusal).
flows.trigger: A scenario or test sets sim.player.alarm_at (e.g. scenarios.lie_detector, tests/test_retreat.py)

steps.text: Decided as each plan is scheduled: a plan already running at the sighting is cut there and answered with alarm.LIE_DETECTOR_ERROR; nothing it has after the cutoff is played.
Any new plan without a kind, and every look of the hunter through client.check_alarm, raises client.LieDetectorAlarm: the hunt stops.

Plans of a kind in alarm.PLAN_KINDS (pet food, retreat, the solver's lie_cursor and lie_ok) go through the real control.player.alarm_refusal; retreat moves are cut at RETREAT_WINDOW_S (12 s) after the sighting, pet food is counted; any other plan is refused.
A plan answered with the alarm raises LieDetectorAlarm from wait, as the real client would.
The scenario looks at the world 10 s after the sighting (whatever the retreat is doing) to check she is on a safe place.

not_done: The game's respawn isn't settled: RESPAWN (8 s per monster) is a guess, and the map's pass with the server's cap is measured on Tree Dungeon only; the map was never seen whole to count its monsters.
DROP_LIFE (180 s), EXPIRE_PASS_S (60 s) and TAKE_RATE (0.05 a minute) are guesses inside what the live evidence bounds.
Which touch-damage form holds on Tree Dungeon (a share of PADamage or meowdb's formula with DEF 75) isn't known; one Horny touch's pixels on her HP bar would tell.
What an arrow held during a knock's flight does isn't measured (KNOCK_STEERS False); whether a knock turns her isn't either (Realism.knock_turns).
An attack picks by each kind's walking height (World.top) while touches use the frame boxes: the two don't agree yet (README: Found offline).
Arrows pressed 0.63-0.78 s after an attack key, and arrows held through the key, are unmeasured for lock_arrows.

Other than lock_arrows and the respawn, none of Realism's knobs is measured (its docstring); the chase (AGGRO_S) and the monsters' AI come from v83 client sources (HeavenClient as RustMS ports it), not this game's own client.
Her HP regeneration isn't kept (for either character); the magician's misses aren't (too few to fit); her MP's extra +9 steps aren't explained.
Whether the game takes a portal in the air, and what happens when she falls below the map's lowest floor, aren't known: the world ends the run either way.
The pets' follow isn't read from the client: a coarse grid fit; the world's pets take 7% of her drops 45-150 units from her where live 23%.
The touch popup's 1 s (POPUP_S) is v83's, unconfirmed in this game; the exact finder's detection rates (NEAR_SEEN_1104) aren't measured live.

No-hit scenes: a verdict holds at the recorded phase, and most shifts don't keep it; 8 of the 11 scenes stay open (strict expected failures) even with the stance fixes for them switched on (GAMELAB_JUMP_ASIDE, GAMELAB_HOP_UP: off by default in play).
